t.4.61.1: Having spoken thus to the best of sages, I wept bitterly, deeply grieved. Then the venerable one, after reflecting for a moment, said this.
t.4.61.2: Your wings and your pinions will grow again, new ones in their place; and your eyes, your vital breaths, your valour and your strength will also be restored to you.
t.4.61.3: For I heard in ancient lore of a very great deed that is yet to come to pass; I have seen it through my austerity as well, and having heard it, I have come to know it.
t.4.61.4: There will be a certain king named Daśaratha, a delight of the Ikṣvāku line; his son, of great splendor, will be named Rāma.
t.4.61.5: And he, of true valour, being appointed to that purpose by his father, will go to the forest together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa.
t.4.61.7: And though she is tempted with every desirable thing, with foods to be chewed and foods to be eaten, Maithilī, the most fortunate and glorious lady, sunk in sorrow, will not eat.
t.4.61.6: A Nairṛta named Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, who cannot be slain by the suras and dānavas, will carry off that one's wife from Janasthāna.
t.4.61.8: Vāsava, having come to know of it through Vaidehī, will give her the finest food, food like amṛta, hard to obtain even for the gods.
t.4.61.9: Having received that food and knowing, "This indeed is from Indra," Maithilī will take out the first portion and offer it on the ground for Rāma.
t.4.61.10: "Whether my husband, the lord, lives together with Lakṣmaṇa, or whether the two of them have attained godhood, this food is for them," thus she spoke.
t.4.61.12: But you must by no means go anywhere; in such a state, where will you go? Wait for the right place and time, and you will regain your wings.
t.4.61.11: Monkeys, Rāma's messengers, will come here searching for her; O bird, you must tell them about Rāma's queen.
t.4.61.13: I could make you winged again this very day, but by remaining here you will accomplish a task that is for the good of the worlds.
t.4.61.14: Indeed, that task must be accomplished by you as well, for the sake of those two princes, of the brāhmaṇas, of the gods, of the sages, and of Vāsava.
t.4.61.15: I too wish to see the two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. I do not wish to sustain my life much longer; I shall abandon this body.
